incident: WannaCry ransomware on NHS England (modelled as one representative infected acute trust), 12 May 2017

sources.title: NAO - Investigation: WannaCry cyber attack and the NHS, HC 414 (full report PDF, 27 Oct 2017)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (internet-facing firewalls / N3, unpatched Windows 7), hop (automatic spread via Windows file-sharing weakness, para 2.9), impact (34 trusts locked out, 46 disrupted, 603 other orgs/595 GP practices, 6,912 confirmed / 19,494 estimated cancellations, 5 A&E diverts, 1,220 infected diagnostic devices incl. MRI), detection timeline (late morning first reports, 13:06 EPRR notified, 16:00 major incident, 18:45 NHS England leads, evening kill-switch), CareCERT alerts 17 Mar and 28 Apr

sources.title: NAO - Investigation: WannaCry cyber attack and the NHS (web summary)
sources.what_it_gave: 80+ of 236 trusts, 603 primary-care orgs, no ransom paid, no patient data stolen, 'could have been prevented by basic IT security best practice'

sources.title: Computing - NHS could have avoided WannaCry simply by patching Windows 7 or securing firewalls, claims NAO
sources.what_it_gave: all infected orgs had unpatched/unsupported Windows; spread via internet incl. N3; no spread via NHSmail; 39 CareCERT alerts

sources.title: National Health Executive - WannaCry cyber-attack cost the NHS £92m after 19,000 appointments were cancelled (DHSC lessons-learned, Feb 2018)
sources.what_it_gave: DHSC cost estimate £92m (£20m lost output during attack, £72m IT restoration), 1% of NHS care disrupted, 8% of GP practices

sources.title: CISA / US-CERT - Alert TA17-181A (Petya) - for MS17-010 context only
sources.what_it_gave: MS17-010 released 14 March 2017 fixes EternalBlue/EternalRomance SMBv1 exploits used by WannaCry and NotPetya

sources.title: NCSC - UK supports US charges against North Korean cyber actors
sources.what_it_gave: attribution of WannaCry to the North Korean (Lazarus) actor
